authors: Daniel Lehmann, Liadan Ita O'Callaghan, and Yoav Shoham

human_review.source: v11 PaperInterface claim surface; human entries are recorded after direct review

human_summary: The auction, greedy approximation, critical-price, and truthfulness results are formalized; Theorem 6.1's native complexity conclusion is an explicit zero-proof partial boundary.
main_caveat: Partial-formalization boundary: reusable runtime composition for Theorem 6.1 is now explicit, and the shared library now has encoding-aware costed-map contracts plus verified unary finite-index, unary-Nat, generic finite-carrier, Boolean-incidence, and finite-set encodings with round trips. The graph reduction now has exact adjacency-input and combined-output size witnesses, including a polynomial bound in encoded input length, and the executable ordered-good representation is proved equivalent to graph-independent-set feasibility. A symmetric loop-free Boolean-table adapter now recovers the corresponding SimpleGraph adjacency exactly, and the typed Boolean-table-to-ordered-incidence PolynomialTimeMap is proved pointwise equal to the executable incidence entries with separate emitted-cell and output-size bounds; encoded feasibility is also proved equivalent to graph-independent selection, while flattened map rows, row-derived feasibility, and the exact emitted-cell work count are proved to have exactly the intended ordered-incidence semantics. These semantic results are exported through ProofInterface. Arbitrary real-valued bids and source-faithful full-reduction step bounds remain IN PROGRESS; native polynomial-time semantics, hardness, approximation, and NP=ZPP consequences remain IN PROGRESS.

open_source_boundaries.description: Finite source/target encodings and output-size bounds are checked, including the executable FiniteGraphTable adjacency code of exact length n*n. A concrete machine step model for the full reduction, arbitrary real-valued bid representation, native hardness/approximation semantics, and the NP=ZPP implication remain unresolved.

llm_statement_review.policy: For every selected source claim, compare only its exact byte-pinned raw source-anchor bundle and Lean's expanded transparent `...Spec : Prop` target. The paired proof endpoint receives separate Lean-Meta proof credit; a name, paraphrase, wrapper, or prior aggregate receipt is not a semantic match. Review every retained paper-local prerequisite and every material library prerequisite before the dependent claim.

title: Truth Revelation in Approximately Efficient Combinatorial Auctions
